title: Go: Immutable Collections
description: Build a persistent immutable vector using structural sharing with Go slices and copy-on-write semantics.

steps.title: Vector struct definition
steps.description: Define a `Vector` struct wrapping an internal `[]interface{}` slice. Write a `New(elements ...interface{}) Vector` constructor and a `Size() int` method. Print the size of a vector created with `New(1, 2, 3)` using `fmt.Println(v.Size())`.
hints: `New` should copy the variadic args into the internal slice.

steps.title: Get and Set with copy-on-write
steps.description: Implement `Get(idx int) (interface{}, bool)` and `Set(idx int, val interface{}) Vector`. Set must return a **new** Vector with the modified element (copy-on-write), leaving the original unchanged. Print the value at index 1 from the original and modified vectors to prove immutability.
hints: `Get` returns `v.data[idx], true` with bounds check, else `nil, false`.
`Set` copies `v.data` into a new slice, mutates the copy, returns a new Vector.
Use `make([]interface{}, len(v.data))` and `copy()` for the clone.

verification.failureMessage: Check Set returns a new Vector without mutating the original.

steps.title: Structural sharing via trie
steps.description: Refactor the Vector to use a 32-ary trie (trie node at each level). Define `node` with `children [32]*node` and `leaf interface{}`. Implement `trieGet` and `trieSet` that share unchanged nodes. Print the value before and after a set to confirm structural sharing works correctly.
hints: Use a `TrieVector` struct with `root *node`, `shift uint`, and `length int`.
`trieSet` clones only the nodes on the path to the leaf, reusing all others.
Use `shift` starting at a high bit (e.g. 32) and decrement by 5 bits per level.

verification.failureMessage: Ensure trieGet and trieSet work with shared nodes.

steps.title: Append and Remove
steps.description: Implement `Append(val interface{}) Vector` and `Remove() Vector`. Append adds at the end; Remove drops the last element. Both return new Vectors without mutation. Print the vector size and last element after an Append followed by a Remove.
hints: Append may need to create a new root if the current trie is full.
Remove decrements length without modifying existing nodes.
Use `fmt.Printf("size=%d last=%v", v.Size(), last)` to display.

verification.failureMessage: Check Append and Remove return new Vectors.

steps.title: Merge
steps.description: Implement `Merge(other Vector) Vector` that returns a new Vector with all elements of the receiver followed by all elements of `other`. Print the merged vector's size and first element to verify correctness.
hints: Iterate `other` and Append each element, or bulk-copy at the trie level.
For simplicity, use a loop calling `Append` on a copy.

verification.failureMessage: Verify Merge returns a new Vector with all elements.

steps.title: ToSlice and FromSlice
steps.description: Implement `ToSlice() []interface{}` (returns a copy of all elements) and a `FromSlice(s []interface{}) Vector` factory. Print the elements of a vector created from `[]interface{}{10, 20, 30}` using a loop with `fmt.Println(v.Get(i))`.
hints: `ToSlice` walks the trie depth-first collecting leaves.
`FromSlice` calls `New(s...)` for flat vectors, or bulk-builds the trie.
Walk and print: `for i := 0; i < v.Size(); i++ { val, _ := v.Get(i); fmt.Println(val) }`.

verification.failureMessage: FromSlice should create a Vector that yields the same elements via ToSlice.
